Sec. 406 of I P C Reads as follows:
Section 406 : Punishment for criminal breach of trust.- Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with both.
Essential ingredients:- an offence under this section has following essential ingredients;
1. Accused was entrusted with some property.
2. Accused had dominion over certain property.

Because he has given the statement along with letter.

It is signed by Binod Tangappa he was his colleague.
16. The PW-1 deposed in his cross examination that the SJ Park Police did not given the letter to him personally asking to give a statement, they gave it to our branch.
He admitted that without seeing the records it is not possible to say whose statement the Police had asked for and what explanation they had asked for.
He don't know about what transaction they had asked for explanation.
He further deposed that he has no information about the cheque, Police have not inquired about it.
They did not give any document to the SJ Park Police station which means he did not give them personally, they sent them C.C.No.5341/2016 through Branch.
He don't know which document were sent from their branch.
He don't know who sent them so he cannot say it is a old case but the said signature belong to Binod.
It is not true that no document goes out of the branch without attention of the Branch Manager when Police asked for information they have to give it.
He further deposed that when the Police asked for information the Branch Manager is more responsibility he was an authorized signatory.

17. The PW-2 is the Branch Manager who has deposed in his chief examination that he was working as Branch Manager Marathahalli Branch, Bengaluru from 2013 to 2015, SJ Park Police issued notice to their branch for providing information their information of account of Narayanaswamy Harish and his two cheques copies.
They have provided both information along with bank statement.
He had issued a letter to the SJ Park Police in which he has been seen the letter issued by him to the SJ Park Police the said letter is marked as Ex.P-1 and his signature is marked as Ex.P1(a).
He has also issued another letter , same is marked as Ex.P-2 and his signature is marked as Ex.P2(a).
He further deposed that he had submitted photo copies of two cheque leaves and one C.C.No.5341/2016 challan to the Police,
Those documents are photo copies.
Hence not marked.
He further deposed that he has also submitted statement of Narayanaswamy, Harish.
The said statement is marked as Ex.P-3 before receiving the document sent the letter he has verified the document then only issued.

18. PW2 deposed in his cross examination that he has received a letter from SJ Park Police Station based upon the said letter he has issued these documents, he has return the letter issued by the Police to the SJ Park Police.

sentences.text: In order to bring home guilt of the accused persons the prosecution has examined 2 witnesses as CW-6 examined as PW-1 and CW-7 examined as PW-2 out of 8 witnesses cited in the charge sheet.
The Learned Sr.APP given up the witness CW-5 was reported died.

This Court made all effort to secure the CW-1 to CW-4 and CW-8 and given sufficient opportunity to them, but in spite of issuance summons, Bailable warrant, NBW and proclamation repeatedly the concerned police not C.C.No.5341/2016 secured the above witnesses, hence this Court dropped the above witnesses.
20. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused person under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused person beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
21. Point No.3: For the reasons stated and finding given to point Nos.1 and 2, the following is made.
ORDER The accused person is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused person is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond executed by him stand canceled.
